s1.syndrome_frame: Facial asymmetry in a neonate with a cerebellopontine angle mass and hearing loss
salient_findings: Enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal on MRI
Profound hearing loss in the left ear on auditory brainstem response testing
key_facts: 4-week-old male patient
Left facial asymmetry observed during crying
Previously passed infant hearing screening
MRI showed an enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal
Follow-up MRI showed considerable growth of the mass
Auditory brainstem response testing demonstrated profound hearing loss in the left ear
Histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity
Biphasic lesion composed of vascular nodules among spindle cells
Glomeruloid-like architecture of vascular epithelial nodules

raw.champion: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE) of the internal auditory canal
raw.rationale: The patient's age, location of the mass, and histopathological findings, including a biphasic lesion with vascular nodules and glomeruloid-like architecture, are consistent with KHE, which is a rare vascular tumor that can occur in the head and neck region, including the internal auditory canal.

rejected.label: Congenital Hemangioblastoma
rejected.why: Hemangioblastomas are typically associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease and have a different histological appearance, with a rich capillary network and stromal cells.

rejected.label: Epithelioid Hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma is a rare vascular tumor that typically occurs in soft tissues and has a distinct histological appearance, with epithelioid endothelial cells and a myxoid stroma, which is not consistent with the patient's histopathological findings.

rejected.label: Infantile hemangioma
rejected.why: Infantile hemangiomas are common benign vascular tumors that typically regress spontaneously, but they do not typically occur in the internal auditory canal and do not have the same histological features as the patient's tumor.

rejected.label: Lymphangioma
rejected.why: Lymphangiomas are benign tumors of the lymphatic system, but the patient's histopathological findings, including the presence of vascular nodules and glomeruloid-like architecture, are not consistent with a lymphangioma.
